timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only Claude CLI stream; semantic events are projected through the raw parent and workflow-child JSONL sources.
Parallel parent read the prompt and README, ran many probes, created task list items, launched the richgo-recon workflow, and continued probing without writing the implementation.
Initial styles-area workflow child received the style parsing brief but produced no semantic work before replacement or interruption.
I/O-area workflow child set up probes and discovered newline behavior, then was interrupted before producing a findings file.
First go-test corpus child built several sample packages and mappings, then was interrupted before delivering the report.
CLI-area child inspected README and tested argv dispatch/fake-go behavior in a short probing run without a report write.
Relaunched go-test corpus child received the brief and was interrupted immediately.
Config-area child ran many .richstyle discovery and precedence probes but did not write a final report in this source.
Short CLI child created a test runner scaffold and was interrupted before completing the CLI report.
Long CLI child ran extensive dispatch, fake-go, stdin, streaming, and signal probes, then was interrupted before writing cli.md.
Go-test corpus child reused existing corpus artifacts and inspected prior outputs without writing a final findings file.

Go-test child scaffolded a richer corpus and was interrupted before capturing and reporting complete corpus outputs.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only Claude CLI stream; semantic events are projected through the raw serial JSONL source.
Serial agent read docs, empirically probed richgo behavior in one trajectory, explored implementation details, but timed out before writing source or compile script.

parallel.requirements: Recognized richgo as a Go test output colorizer to be reimplemented from observed CLI behavior and README documentation only.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Created task-list items for behavior areas, implementation, and differential testing, then launched a workflow whose executed children owned only behavior-area research reports.
parallel.implementation: No replacement source implementation was written; the parent and children stayed in empirical probing and report generation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No implementation components were integrated or assembled; artifact validation listed only the original workspace files and no buildable replacement.
parallel.verification: Many reference-binary probes were run, but there was no generated executable to verify against the acceptance suite.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out before implementation, compile script, integrated tests, or final delivery; official evaluation failed at compile time with all 787 tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room richgo reimplementation requirements and used only local execution and documentation for behavioral discovery.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept the whole task in one trajectory with no workflows or subagents, probing behavior serially before attempting implementation.
serial.implementation: The agent accumulated many behavior rules and stated an intent to write pure-Go stdlib code, but continued probing and did not create a buildable replacement.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No final source tree or compile script was assembled; artifact validation contained only the original workspace files.
serial.verification: Reference-behavior probes were extensive, including CLI, config, styling, and line parsing, but no replacement executable was tested.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out with no delivered implementation; official evaluation reported compile_failed with 0 of 787 tests run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the task as clean-room behavioral reimplementation of the provided richgo binary and documentation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering task and the same prohibitions on source lookup and wrapping.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference; both focused on observing the executable, not external source.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created task-list items and launched a workflow whose executed child work was behavior probing, critique, and gap filling.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows disabled and no delegation; all reconnaissance and implementation intent remained in one agent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel externalized investigation to many children but did not activate an implementation owner, while serial used no child ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were detailed research briefs for separate behavior areas and instructed children to write notes under /tmp/rg/findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept observed behavior and interface assumptions in one continuous context without handoff contracts between agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced research handoffs and shared notes, but no cross-agent implementation interface needed reconciliation because no implementation components were produced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed extensive probing and one child wrote a styles findings file, but no source implementation or compile script appeared in the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also performed extensive probing and stated it would write pure-Go stdlib code, but kept probing and did not deliver implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both failed on missing implementation; the parallel-specific difference is that executed child work remained investigative rather than implementation-producing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Several workflow children were interrupted or relaunched, and the parent never received a completed end-to-end workflow result before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; its lifecycle failure was simply that the single process timed out mid-analysis.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child-result lifecycle churn, while serial had none; both still closed without a deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children and the parent shared /tmp/rg scratch and findings paths, but no generated implementation was available to integrate.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used its own scratch files and sample modules in a single stream and likewise never integrated a final tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared state existed mainly for research notes; no live source-merge collision or integrated implementation was observed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified many observed behaviors of the reference binary but had no candidate implementation to run through integrated acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise verified reference behavior extensively but never reached evaluator-aligned validation of a generated executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification differed in organization, not final acceptance: neither checked a replacement against the test suite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out at the cell budget with 17 workflow child logs and a SIGTERM return code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial timed out at the same budget with workflows disabled and only Bash tool calls.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent budget across parent plus children; serial spent it in one long local investigation. Both closed by timeout.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed the same way: compile_failed with 0/787 tests run. The parallel run differed by using a large workflow of research children and never activating implementation ownership, while the serial run kept the work local and also kept probing until timeout. The shared outcome is best explained by no delivered buildable reimplementation in either run, not by an evaluator discrepancy or a successful path in one mode.
parallel_contributors: Executed workflow scope stayed in behavior research, critique, and gap filling rather than source implementation.
The run timed out with 17 workflow child logs and no buildable artifact.
serial_contributors: Single-agent trajectory spent the budget on increasingly detailed behavior probes.
The run also timed out before source, compile script, or integrated validation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Neither mode produced enough implementation for ordinary algorithmic differences to be evaluated.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluations stopped at compile_failed before running any of the 787 tests.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained label describes a realized parallel process failure but not a discordant official result

candidates.reason: The executed parallel allocation put children on behavior-area reports and workflow critique/fill phases, while the implementation task was never activated as live child or parent work before timeout.
candidates.realized_consequence: No generated implementation or compile script was present when the parallel run closed, so the official evaluator failed at compile time and ran 0 of 787 tests.
candidates.near_match_reason: The workflow was investigation-first, but the decisive fix would be assigning active implementation ownership rather than merely shortening a completed investigation phase.

Rejected: the workflow had broad fan-out, but the adverse result is classified at the earlier no-implementation-owner boundary rather than child-count exhaustion.
Rejected: no single child carried the indispensable implementation; children were scoped to research areas and most incompletion was part of the same research workflow.
Rejected: child briefs intentionally asked for behavior research notes; missing implementation was not an omitted known requirement within an executed implementation child brief.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Serial Investigation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Early Child Termination, Blind Timeout Wait, and No Failure Takeover were considered downstream or near-match descriptions of the same research-workflow/no-implementation chain and were not separately retained.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the no-active-implementation-owner boundary cleared the retention gate as an independent parallel coordination pattern.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: One pattern was retained to avoid multiplying the same workflow timeout chain across allocation, timing, retry, and monitoring labels.
